summary: A list of correct front-panel switch settings for IMPs and TIPs, written because wrong settings had caused problems. It covers the 516 IMPs and the 316 IMPs and TIPs, and says the RFC will be updated when settings change.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 395 lists front-panel switch settings for two kinds of IMPs and for TIPs. It asks site staff to check the settings and keep the list near the equipment.

subtitle: A checklist of front-panel switch settings for IMPs and TIPs

tldr.problem: Incorrect switch settings on network equipment had caused operational difficulties.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists the correct settings for Model 516 IMPs and Model 316 IMPs and TIPs.
tldr.outcome: Sites and field engineers are asked to keep the note near the equipment and use it as a checklist.

today: RFC 395 is an operational checklist for switch settings on specified IMP and TIP models. It says the guidance would be updated when settings changed.

sections.title: Why the Switch List Was Issued
sections.content: The RFC says that incorrect front-panel switch settings on IMPs and TIPs had caused difficulties. It provides a checklist for site personnel and says the document would be updated if the settings changed.
sections.plainLanguage: Some equipment problems had been caused by switches set incorrectly. The note records the settings staff should check.

sections.title: Settings for Model 516 IMPs
sections.content: The RFC identifies a Model 516 by its gray cabinet and two rows of front-panel indicator lights. It lists settings for sense switches 1 through 4, PFI/PFH, HALT INH, W.D.T., AUTO RSTRT and MEMORY PRTCT. The listed settings are OFF for the sense switches, PFI, OFF for HALT INH and W.D.T., ON for AUTO RSTRT, and OFF for MEMORY PRTCT.
sections.plainLanguage: For a Model 516, the RFC gives a specific position for each listed switch. Staff can use the checklist to compare the front panel with those settings.

sections.title: Settings for Model 316 IMPs and TIPs
sections.content:
The RFC identifies a Model 316 as a TIP or as an IMP in a black cabinet with one row of indicator lights. For these units, it lists sense switches 1 through 4 as OFF, with the top half depressed.

Site personnel are asked to keep a copy near the IMP, and Honeywell field engineers are asked to use it during preventive maintenance.
sections.plainLanguage: For Model 316 equipment, check that sense switches 1 through 4 are OFF. The note asks staff to keep the list near the equipment for maintenance.
